subject: POC success criteria & burst profile intake — SparkRetail
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@sparkretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T15:22:00-04:00
Subject: Recap + next steps from today’s POC call

Hi Elena — thanks again for the conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before the kickoff: 

Call summary:
- Goal: run a 2-week POC to validate latency, cost, and extraction quality on SparkRetail’s product-search assistant (query rewriting + reranking).
- Primary success criteria discussed: p95 generation latency <= 450ms, retrieval/intent accuracy lift >= 6% vs baseline, and a cost-per-1k-queries target under $X (we’ll refine).

Traffic profile (you mentioned rough numbers on the call):
- Baseline steady-state: ~8 RPS
- Typical concurrency: 25–40 concurrent sessions for the assistant flows
- Token distribution: prompts ~35–80 tokens; responses ~60–210 tokens (median ~120 tokens)
- Burst behavior: daily promotions can spike to ~140 RPS for 3–8 minutes; weekend promos less predictable but rarer.

Next steps I propose:
1) Please complete the attached "poc-intake-template.xlsx" with a 72‑hour sampling of traffic (or provide the workload-sample.jsonl) so we can build an ingest profile and sizing suggestion.
2) Technical kickoff: Fri Apr 23, 10:00 AM PT (30–45m). I’ll send a calendar invite with an infra checklist.
3) Redwood will deliver a one-page evaluation plan and a baseline latency/cost estimate within 48 hours of receiving the sample.

Owners on our side: Karthik (SE lead / sales follow-up), Marissa (Customer Success / onboarding), Sean (Infra & runtime sizing).

Attachment: poc-intake-template.xlsx (attachment stub — excel).

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Park <elena@sparkretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@sparkretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today’s POC call

Thanks Karthik — that looks right to me. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The baseline 8 RPS is what our search service sees today for assistant queries; the app-level concurrency you suggested (25–40) is accurate because of long user sessions.
- Burst explanation: promotional emails drive quick spikes; the largest we saw during last year’s holiday test hit ~160 RPS for ~6 minutes.
- Token lengths: your numbers match our telemetry samples. We’ll try to extract a 72‑hour window and drop it into your intake template by EOD Thu (Apr 22).

One ask: can Redwood provision a canary variant (smaller-capacity) we can hit immediately for functional validation, then scale to the sizing you recommend?

Tom and I are available for the Fri kickoff.

—Elena
VP Product, SparkRetail
Elena Park <elena@sparkretail.com>

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@sparkretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-21T08:04:00-04:00
Subject: POC plan, success metrics, and intake items (action required)

Elena / Tom — great, thanks for confirming. Below is the POC plan I’ll bring to the kickoff; please treat items in BOLD as actions for SparkRetail before we begin.

POC scope (2 weeks)
- Week 0 (pre-kickoff): intake + traffic sample + NDA/tech contacts (complete)
- Week 1: baseline measurements with canary model (functional + latency tests)
- Week 2: optimization pass (batching, prefix cache, quantization suggestions where acceptable) and evaluation against success criteria

Success criteria (finalized during kickoff) — proposed:
- Latency: p95 <= 450ms, p99 <= 900ms for conversational flows under expected concurrency
- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% over test window
- Quality: intent/intent-classifier F1 lift >= 6% and rerank NDCG@5 improvement >= 4% vs baseline
- Cost: estimated tokens/1k-queries under $Y (will provide estimate after sample)

Evaluation plan
- Redwood will run the sample traffic against the canary model for a 48-hour baseline window; we’ll measure latency, token counts, and KV cache hit rates.
- We’ll run a controlled promotional burst test (you provide a replay or synthetic generator) to validate autoscaling and tail latency under 1.5–2x observed peak.
- Quality tests: Redwood will score a 2k-item holdout (you can provide labels) to calculate the quality deltas.

Required intake items (BOLD = action)
- COMPLETE & RETURN: poc-intake-template.xlsx with a 72‑hour sample (timestamps in UTC)
- OPTIONAL: workload-sample.jsonl with anonymized queries (we can accept truncated tokens).
- PROVIDE: a labeled holdout of ~2k items (CSV) for quality measurement (or permit Redwood to apply lightweight heuristics if labels not available).

Timeline and milestone owners
- Thu Apr 22: receive intake files (SparkRetail action)
- Fri Apr 23 10:00 AM PT: technical kickoff (attendees: Karthik, Marissa, Sean, Elena, Tom) — calendar invite to follow
- Mon Apr 26: Redwood baseline results + sizing recommendation
- Fri May 7: final POC report (includes cost model and recommended next steps)

Canary + immediate functional validation: yes, we can spin a small canary capacity (single-GPU variant with reduced tokens) the day after we receive the sample — useful to smoke test integration. Note that performance scaling will change once we move to the optimized config.

Attachment (uploaded): workload-sample.jsonl (stub) — we used a sanitized example to validate the schema.

Let me know if any of the success criteria should be adjusted before the kickoff. I’ll send the calendar invite shortly.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: workload-sample.jsonl (jsonl stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Elena — thanks for committing to EOD delivery of the intake. Once we have it I’ll run our onboarding checklist and share the access matrix.

—Marissa
